title.narrative: One-off winter cash assistance for newly arrived vulnerable Sundanese refugees

description.narrative: The UNHCR intervention will seek to scale up financial support to the most vulnerable new arrivals from Sudan in Egypt, with particular focus on addressing heightened needs during the cold winter months. UNHCR will provide cash assistance for winter needs with an average transfer value of USD 160 for a family of 3 to 4 people, as an average size. This assistance will be distributed to some 14,650 new arrival most vulnerable families, comprising of around 50,300 individuals on the waiting list and identified as extremely poor. Household assessments are conducted through a Vulnerability Assessment (VA) that applies a proxy means testing formula, using the national poverty line as a threshold. UNHCR will provide one-time winter cash assistance that covers 75% of the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) calculated using CAPMAS data, the government statistical organization. This support will cover three months of essential winter needs, including electricity costs, clothing, blankets, and an electric heater, with the overarching aim to reduce protection risks and the adoption of negative coping strategies. The UNHCR midyear Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) report highlights the main spending priorities for Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA). The most frequently cited expenditure was for food (83%), followed by rent (67%), health expenses (19%), utilities (10%), and infant items (5%). These findings reflect the critical role cash assistance plays in enabling refugees and asylum seekers to cover their most pressing basic needs during increasingly difficult economic conditions. UNHCR is not assisting host communities due to the high needs refugees are facing, as per the Office's mandate, and the limited resources available. Moreover, vulnerable host community already benefit from national social protection programmes. To ensure the effective delivery of cash assistance and avoid duplication, UNHCR actively collaborates with other actors through the Egypt Cash Working Group under the Refugee Coordination Model (RCM). Regular meetings, including those under the Deduplication Task Force, focus on coordinating efforts, aligning targeting strategies, and ensuring that cash support reaches the most vulnerable households efficiently and equitably. This coordination strengthens the collective impact of cash-based interventions while promoting accountability and optimal resource allocation adjusting the response according to the trends and needs.
